Barcelona's 22-man travelling squad leaves out Lamine Yamal (ankle, kept back as a precaution), Rodri, Xavi Espart, Christensen and Roony Bardghji; the numbers now count Yamal, Rodri, Espart and Christensen. Pau Cubarsí is back after missing the Villarreal game and Marc Bernal travels, and neither the club nor the Spanish press points to big rotation, so my earlier trim for rotation no longer holds. Aden McCarthy's ban for Sabah is counted. Scottish referee Nick Walsh is in charge; his high card rate (5.8 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals (1.2 Sabah, 3.1 Barcelona), now taking off Lamine Yamal (-16.7%), who provides about a fifth of Barcelona's goal involvement, plus Rodri, Espart and Christensen, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. The squad that travelled is otherwise near full strength, with Raphinha, Pedri, Olmo and Cubarsí, so I drop my -4% rotation trim and stay at 4.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona as the side that will have most of the ball against a compact Sabah block. Without Yamal, Barcelona's width comes from Adeyemi and Gordon, which still pushes play to the flanks, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card count (+25.9%) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+11.5%), which fits a side chasing the ball all night, and taking off Barcelona's quieter spell (-4.7%). That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry, and I see nothing beyond it, so I stay at 5.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), already lifted for Barcelona's heavy recent shooting (+10.6%). Yamal is a big source of Barcelona's shots, which the numbers only take off goals, but Sabah's confidence after a 5-1 win and a full stadium could make them braver and the game more open; these pull both ways, so I stay at 34.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's sharp recent finishing (+8.5%). Without clear signs of rotation the travel and Yamal's absence are the only small points against, and Sabah's attacking intent points the other way, so I stay at 12.3.

401915293.overall: Slavia are 34th of 36 with 1 point and Villarreal 28th with 3, so both are below the top-24 line and need a win; Slavia have never beaten a Spanish club in the Champions League proper but lead the Czech league after a 2-0 win at Olomouc. Slavia are without Štěpán Chaloupek, David Moses, Elias Piták and Danijel Šturm as well as the counted Adonija Ouanda, and Lukáš Provod (illness from international duty, listed by UEFA with a tendon problem) is a doubt; only Ouanda and Ogbu are in the numbers. Villarreal lost 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday after leading 2-0 and are still without Gerard Moreno, Juan Foyth and Ilias Akhomach, which the numbers do not count, plus the counted Alassane Diatta; Mouriño is one booking from a ban. Absences on both sides roughly cancel out, so the view stays with the numbers. Slovenian referee Rade Obrenović is in charge, with a slightly low card record that is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals (1.2 Slavia, 2.4 Villarreal), already counting both sides' recent scoring and Diatta's absence. Villarreal are still without Gerard Moreno and Akhomach up front, while Slavia lose Moses and maybe Provod from midfield; both teams need a win, so these pull both ways and I stay at 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised for Slavia's recent corner count (+5.7%). Slavia attack down the flanks with wing-backs Vlček and Jurásek and Villarreal like wide play with Buchanan and Moleiro; that is the game the numbers expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already taking off Slavia's unusually low recent card count (-9.8%) and Rade Obrenović's slightly low record (-2.1%), and adding Villarreal's high one (+5.3%). Two teams that both need the result can make for a tense game, but there is no bad blood, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15.9% Slavia, +8.2% Villarreal). Slavia's high-tempo home game fits that picture; Villarreal's missing attackers could cut a little, but they still scored twice at Barcelona, so I stay at 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already counting Slavia's sharper recent finishing (+11.2%). With uncounted absences on both sides (Moses and Provod for Slavia, Gerard Moreno and Akhomach for Villarreal) I see nothing that tips it, so I stay at 10.1.

401915291.overall: Atlético Madrid (23rd, 4 points) and Viking (22nd, 4 points) sit one place apart and both need points to stay in the play-off places; it is the clubs' first meeting. Atlético lost 2-0 at home to Bayern last time in Europe but beat Getafe 3-0 on Sunday; Lookman (knee) and Romero (muscle) are out, and Marc Pubill (ankle) is back in partial training but listed out by UEFA, with Le Normand and Hancko expected at centre-back. The numbers count Lookman and Pubill, and Romero's long absence is already in Atlético's form. Viking, the Norwegian champions, beat Sabah 4-1, have scored in 12 European games in a row and are without Bærtelsen, Bjørshol, D'Agostino and Roseth (all counted), with Berisha and Haugen doubtful. Belgian referee Erik Lambrechts (2.9 cards a game) is named and already counted; I found nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, 2.6 of them Atlético's, and already take Lookman and Pubill off Atlético (about -2% each) while adding 6% to Viking for Pubill missing at the back. Julián Álvarez and Sørloth are expected up front, and Viking's top scorer Peter Christiansen (19 this season) is fit, so both attacks are as the numbers assume. If Pubill makes it after all, that would trim Viking's side slightly, but he is not expected to; I stay at 3.9.

corners.text: The numbers expect 11.8 corners, about 8 of them Atlético's, who should have most of the ball at home against a side that rarely wins away in Europe. Viking's busy recent corner count already adds about 3% to their side and Atlético's quieter run takes 1.5% off theirs. Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone on the flanks fit that picture, so I stay at about 12.

cards.text: The numbers expect 2.9 cards, already cut about 17% for referee Erik Lambrechts, who shows 2.9 a game, and a little for both sides' recent counts. There is no rivalry and Viking are an open, attacking side rather than a cynical one, so nothing points either way and I stay at 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.1 shots, 21 of them Atlético's, and already add about 14% to Viking's side for their recent shooting against a leaky Atlético. Atlético at home with Álvarez, Sørloth, Baena and possibly Lee Kang-in should shoot plenty, which is the usual picture, so I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11 shots on target and already take about 2% off Atlético for their accuracy lately. Lookman is in the numbers' missing list, and the rest of Atlético's front line is fit, while Viking keep finding the target in Europe; I stay at 11.

401915292.overall: Club Brugge (9th) and Liverpool (8th) are level on 9 points, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Brugge have won their last three in Europe and won 5-1 at Mechelen on Saturday, with Nicolò Tresoldi (five Champions League goals) leading the line; Joel Ordóñez (foot, counted) and Jan Virgili (groin) are doubts. Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday but lost 3-2 at Fenerbahçe last time in Europe; Ekitiké (counted), Leoni and Bradley are out, and UEFA and ESPN both now list Cody Gakpo out with a muscle injury, which the numbers do not know, while Gravenberch is a doubt. Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández Hernández (4.9 cards a game) is named and the numbers already add about 28% to cards for him. My only move since the last view is a small cut on goals for Gakpo.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, 1.8 of them Liverpool's, already up a little for both attacks' form. Gakpo, one of Liverpool's regular scorers, is out with a muscle injury that the numbers don't list, so I take about 3% off, to about 3.3. Isak, Wirtz (five goals in his last four games) and Barcola are fit, which keeps the cut small.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.3 corners, 6 of them Liverpool's, and already add about 5% for Liverpool's high corner count lately. Liverpool's wide play with Ngumoha and Muñoz or Barcola should look as usual even without Gakpo, and Brugge sit compact at home, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4 cards and already add about 28% for referee Hernández Hernández, who averages 4.9 a game, plus 5% for Brugge's busy recent card count. There is no rivalry and nothing else points either way, so I stay at 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.8 shots and have already pushed both sides up by 15-19% for their recent shooting. Gakpo's absence changes who shoots for Liverpool more than how often, so I see no reason to move and stay at about 35.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 shots on target, already up about 9% for both sides' recent accuracy. Tresoldi is in form for Brugge and Liverpool still have Isak and Wirtz, so beyond the small goals cut for Gakpo I stay at about 12.

401915376.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday after giving up three two-goal leads; Lautaro Martínez came back with a late cameo and is expected to start, but Hakan Çalhanoğlu is now out with a thigh problem from that game (UEFA and Sports Mole; another preview calls him questionable), and Bonny (counted) is out. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Stiller (groin, counted out), Jaquez and Sauer are doubts, and Demirović (four Champions League goals) leads the line. French referee François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted. Lautaro's return and Çalhanoğlu's absence pull Inter's goals in opposite directions, so I drop my earlier small lift and stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take Bonny off Inter and Stiller off Stuttgart (about -4% each). Lautaro starting adds to Inter's attack, but losing Çalhanoğlu, their penalty and set-piece taker, takes some of that back, and neither is in the numbers. They roughly cancel out, so I drop my earlier +3% and stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.1 corners, 6.2 of them Inter's, already up 6% for Inter's recent corner count. Dimarco and Spence are fit on the flanks and Stuttgart play a wing-back system too, which fits the usual picture, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.7 cards and already take a little off Inter for their quiet recent record and for referee Letexier, who sits near the average at 4.0 a game. Çalhanoğlu, who was one booking from a ban, won't play, and there is no rivalry, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.4 shots and already add about 20% to Inter's side for their recent shooting and take 7% off Stuttgart's. Inter at home with Lautaro and Esposito should shoot plenty, but that is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, up 7% for Inter's accuracy lately and down 3% for Stuttgart's. Lautaro back sharpens Inter, while Çalhanoğlu's long shots are lost, so I stay at about 10.6.

401915377.overall: Lille are 35th with 1 point from 4 games and lost 1-0 at home to Lyon on Friday, so this is close to their last chance of the play-offs; Tiago Santos and Igamane are out (counted), Nianzou is a doubt and Ethan Mbappé returns from a ban. Bayern (13th, 8 points) drew 1-1 with Köln and are badly hit: Harry Kane had ankle surgery and is out for about three months, and Gnabry, Saibari, Davies and Neuer are out too. The numbers' missing list no longer includes Kane, so his absence is not in them now; Michael Olise (bruised foot, on crutches at the weekend) also missed Monday's training and Bild calls his return increasingly unlikely, which the numbers don't know either. German press expect 18-year-old Lennart Karl through the middle, with Luis Díaz and Musiala possible. Italian referee Marco Guida (3.6 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.7 of them Bayern's, and take Gnabry, Saibari and Davies off but no longer list Kane. Without Kane, their main scorer, and very likely Olise, Bayern's attack loses its two biggest sources of goals, so I take 12% off the match, to about 2.5. Lille have been short of goals too (none against Lyon), and Díaz possibly returning is what keeps me from going further.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.7 corners, split almost evenly. A makeshift Bayern front line may be less dangerous but should still have the ball, while Lille must push for a win at home; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3 cards, already cut about 12% for referee Marco Guida's low card count and 12% for Bayern's quiet recent record. Lille's must-win mood could add a booking late on, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.

shots.text: The numbers say 25 shots, nearly 15 from Bayern, and the missing-player adjustment does not touch shots anyway. Kane and Olise are Bayern's two most frequent shooters, and a young line led by Lennart Karl should create less; Lille needing a win stops me going further, so about 23.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Without Kane and probably Olise, Bayern lose their best finishers, and the numbers count neither, so I go down to about 8.4.

401915374.overall: PSG are top of the league phase with 12 points and 20 goals from 4 games and have won 12 in a row, most recently 3-2 at Nice; Roma are 20th with 4 points and at risk of going out early, though they are unbeaten in Serie A and beat Parma 5-1 with four goals from Donyell Malen. PSG lost Désiré Doué to a serious right knee injury at Nice and Kvaratskhelia is out with a torn ACL; the numbers count both, and Dembélé, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are back. Roma have Svilar and Dybala back, Pellegrini is out (counted), and Rensch and Balerdi are doubts. Swedish referee Glenn Nyberg (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted. I found nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, lifted by both teams' scoring form (about +6% PSG, +4% Roma) and taking Doué (-6%) and Kvaratskhelia (-4%) off PSG. Dembélé is back to lead PSG's attack and Malen is in form for Roma, which fits that picture, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Roma's busy recent corner count already adding about 3%. PSG will have most of the ball and Gasperini's Roma attack wide with wing-backs Wesley and Molina, but nothing in the team news changes how many corners either side wins, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already cut about 10% for referee Glenn Nyberg's low card count and for both sides' quiet recent records (PSG only 3 in their last 6). Roma's man-to-man pressing tends to draw fouls against a side that keeps the ball, which is why their share is larger; with no rivalry or suspension angle, I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots, with both sides' high recent shot counts already adding 9-11%. Losing Doué costs PSG a shooter, but Dembélé is back to take that role and PSG should dominate the ball at home, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 13.1 shots on target, pushed up by PSG's very accurate recent run (+22%). Doué is in the numbers' missing list, and Svilar returning in Roma's goal doesn't change how many shots reach it, so I stay at 13.1.

401915375.overall: Shakhtar (21st, 4 points) host Fenerbahçe (19th, 5 points) at Stamford Bridge in London because of the war, so there is little real home advantage; both need points to stay in play-off contention. Shakhtar, under Arda Turan, are winless in three and without Pedrinho (counted, -14% on their goals) and young striker Kauã Elias (foot fracture), whom UEFA lists out and the numbers don't; Marlon Gomes is expected to play and is one booking from a ban. Fenerbahçe, under Emre Belözoğlu, beat Liverpool 3-2 last time in Europe and drew 2-2 at Kocaelispor; Aké (counted), Oosterwolde and Asensio (out since October, already in their form) are missing, while Lukaku is fit again. English referee Michael Oliver (4.0 cards a game) is named and already counted. My only moves are small cuts for Elias.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take Pedrinho off Shakhtar (-14%) while adding 6% for Aké missing at Fenerbahçe's back. Kauã Elias's foot fracture is not in the numbers, but he has missed a few games already, so I trim only a little, to about 2.6. Lukaku being fit again for Fenerbahçe keeps me from going further.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already raised about 12% for Shakhtar's busy recent corner count and trimmed 9% for Fenerbahçe's. A ground in London takes some of Shakhtar's home push away, but nothing in the team news points clearly either way, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, a high figure that reflects Fenerbahçe's card-heavy style (about 3 a game) and both sides' records, with referee Michael Oliver near the average at 4.0 a game. Both sides need the points and Marlon Gomes plays one booking from a ban, but the numbers already carry that style, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, with Shakhtar's recent shooting run already adding about 15% to their side and Fenerbahçe's trimmed 9%. Elias's loss shows more in finishing than in volume, and Lukaku returning helps Fenerbahçe's, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Kauã Elias, which the numbers don't see, Shakhtar lean more on Alisson Santana and the wide players, who have been wasteful in Europe, so I trim slightly, to about 8.5.

401915373.overall: Sporting (10th, 9 points) host Manchester United (17th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting close to the top eight, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game was a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match UEFA ban for his red card against Roma) and Marcus Rashford (hip), neither of whom the numbers list, plus Šeško, Baleba and Ugarte (counted); Shaw is a doubt, and Yoro is available because his ban is domestic only. Sporting miss Debast and Nuno Santos but have Ioannidis and Flávio Gonçalves back in training. Polish referee Szymon Marciniak (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take Šeško off United (-4.5%). Cunha is banned and Rashford is out with a hip problem, two of United's main attackers that the numbers don't know about, so I take about 7% off, to about 2.7. United's leaky defence (19 conceded in 6) is already in the numbers, and Sporting getting Ioannidis back keeps me from going further.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with United slightly more of them. Fonseca's Sporting build through the middle and Pochettino has had only days to change anything, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already lowered about 9% for referee Marciniak's low card count and 11% for Sporting's quiet recent record, and raised 4% for United's busy one. Cunha's ban removes one hot-headed player, but that is small, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with United's recent shot volume adding about 9% to their side. Without Cunha and Rashford, two of their busiest shooters, and with Šeško out, United's attack rests on Mbeumo, Fernandes and Zirkzee, so I trim a little, to about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, split evenly. Cunha's ban and Rashford's injury, which the numbers don't see, take away two of United's main finishers, so I trim slightly, to about 10.

401915816.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points from three games) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty on matchday 4 and need a win to climb out of the elimination places after a 1-1 draw at Atalanta, their only point-winning European display under interim coach Zhora Harutyunyan, who took over when Rafael Urazbakhtin left in late October. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they come in with about three weeks without a competitive game, and their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers. Mjällby are fresher and still playing league football: they drew 1-1 with Malmö on 21 November, but forward Jacob Bergström was replaced after 41 minutes of that game, reported yesterday as a thigh strain and still unconfirmed for this trip, while Dalsgaard and Stavitski (already in the numbers) stay out. One preview expects Mjällby to rotate with a league game three days later; no referee is named yet and specific Kairat team news remains thin, so the view leans only slightly lower on shooting and will be refreshed nearer kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Kairat's long break could blunt their attack but also loosen a defence that let in five at home to Panathinaikos, while a missing Bergström or a rotated Mjällby side points slightly down, so with these pulling both ways I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for their recent 17 in three. Kairat will want to push at home, but Mjällby as the fresher, in-season side can keep the ball, which the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already shows, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, with Mjällby's tidy recent record taking a little off. No referee has been named and there is no rivalry or bad-tempered history between the clubs; a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 4.5 until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.1, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach, and Mjällby may be without Bergström (off after 41 minutes against Malmö) and could rotate before a league game; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. Kairat's lack of match rhythm since their league season ended and the doubt over Bergström, Mjällby's main aerial threat, point a little lower, so I go to about 8.1.

401915815.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points), and the numbers make Ajax big favourites: they are unbeaten in seven, beat ADO Den Haag 3-0 on Sunday with 79% of the ball and 21 shots, and won 6-1 at Midtjylland in this competition. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys at the weekend and have not kept a clean sheet in 13 games; FotMob lists five Thun players out, including defender Genís Montolio (cruciate ligament, until January), none of them in the numbers' missing list, though most have been out for a while and so are already in Thun's recent form. Ajax are still without Dolberg (cruciate), Adingra and Tsygankov, all long absences the form already reflects, and they go to Feyenoord for De Klassieker on Sunday 29 November, so changes to the Ajax side are likely; Thun also play a league game three days later. No referee is named yet. I keep a small cut on goals and shots for the expected Ajax rotation and leave the rest alone.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, 3.2 of them for Ajax, and they already add 4% for Ajax's 16 goals in their last six and Thun's leaky defence. With De Klassieker at Feyenoord three days later, Míchel is likely to rest some of the side that started against ADO (Arokodare, Gloukh, Klaassen), so I trim 4%, to about 4.0 goals. Thun's missing defenders, Montolio among them, have been out for weeks and are already in their 13 games without a clean sheet.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 6.5 of them Ajax's, against a Thun side that has about 39% of the ball on average. Rotation changes who plays more than how Ajax play: even a changed side had 8 corners against ADO. Recent corner form is already in, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.6) chasing the ball, and both sides' recent bookings are already in. No referee has been named, and nothing points to a heated night between two sides with no rivalry. I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, about 20 of them Ajax's, and already add 3% for Ajax's recent volume (21 shots against ADO). A rotated Ajax side three days before Feyenoord away is likely to slow the game once it is won, so I take off 3%, to about 29.5 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already take about 6% off Thun's side for their weak recent accuracy. For the same Ajax rotation reason I trim 3%, to about 9.3. Thun's injured players are mostly long-term and already in their form.

401915814.overall: Brighton (5th of 36, 7 points) host Universitatea Craiova (8th, also 7 points) in a game that matters for a top-eight finish for both. Brighton come in after a 2-0 defeat at Hull on Sunday, with two stoppage-time goals conceded after Costinha's red card (a league ban, so it does not stop him here), and they play Newcastle at the weekend, so rotation is likely as usual in this competition. Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas and Yohanna are out and are now in the numbers' missing list, while Azeez, Struijk and Chema Andrés are fit again and Minteh is fine after international duty, with Hadjam unclear. Craiova, top of the Romanian league after a 6-2 win at UTA Arad, have named a settled eleven; one report says centre-back Nikola Stevanovic was hurt in a friendly on 16 November and Cicâldău took a knock at Arad, but neither absence is confirmed. No referee is named; with the absences now counted, I keep only a small cut on Brighton's attack for rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.9 of them for Brighton; Mitoma, Ferguson, Tzimas and Yohanna are now in their missing list, and they already take 3% off for Brighton scoring only 4 in their last six. What they can't see is a rotated Brighton side between Hull and Newcastle, so I trim 3%, to about 3.4 goals. That is a smaller cut than yesterday's 5% because the absences are now counted and Azeez and Struijk are back.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, 8.2 of them for Brighton. Even a changed Brighton side will keep the ball and push Craiova back, which is what the numbers expect. I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already up a little for both sides' recent bookings, with Craiova (2.6) expected to collect more chasing the game. No referee has been named and Costinha's red at Hull only carries a league ban. I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, almost 22 of them Brighton's, and already add 2% for Brighton's recent volume (they had plenty of chances at Hull). A rotated side should create a little less, so I take off 3%, to about 27.9 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target and already take 8% off Brighton for poor recent accuracy, with the injured attackers also counted. Rotation points slightly the same way, so I take off 2%, to about 10.3.

401915810.overall: Egnatia (26th of 36, 2 points) host Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, 3 points) at the Air Albania Stadium in Tirana, and the club has sold cheap tickets to fill the ground for what it sees as its best chance of a first win in the competition. Egnatia lost 1-0 at Skënderbeu at the weekend but stay top in Albania; defender Enea Bitri is suspended after two yellow cards, which the numbers already count. Lincoln beat Hajduk Split 1-0 but lost to Brann and Twente and have been weaker away; FotMob lists defender Ethan Jolley as doubtful with a leg injury, the only Lincoln news I found. Both sides rotate often, which is already in their recent form, and no referee is named. News was thin, so the view rests on form and context and I make no change.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already add about 6% to Lincoln's side because Bitri, a regular in Egnatia's defence, is suspended. Egnatia promise to attack at home, but they have also drawn tight games with Midtjylland and AGF, and Jolley's doubt for Lincoln is too uncertain to move anything. I stay at 3.1.

Hearts arrive on a high after an 8-0 win at Dundee on Saturday (against ten men from the second half), with Kerjota and Kabore scoring twice each, even though McEntee, Walcott and a long list of others are injured; the numbers already count those absences, including a large cut for McEntee. Monaco are without Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo-Muzambo, now in the numbers' missing list, plus defender Elebi according to one team-news site; they are winless in six Ligue 1 games but have a perfect European record, and they go to Lyon three days later, so rotation is likely. Hearts face Celtic next. No referee is named; the changes since yesterday's view are now in the numbers, so I make no change.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.3 of them for Monaco; they now take off for Golovin and Idumbo-Muzambo and cut Hearts' side by a quarter for McEntee. Hearts just scored eight without McEntee, which suggests that cut is generous, while a rotated Monaco side before Lyon points the other way; the two roughly cancel. I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, split almost evenly. Hearts at home, needing a result and in scoring form, will push forward, while Monaco usually have more of the ball; the numbers already capture that balance and both sides' recent corner counts. I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already low for Monaco's few recent bookings. No referee is named and nothing I read points to a bad-tempered night. I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and already take 6% off Monaco for their lower recent shot output. Hearts' confidence after the 8-0 could add a few home shots against a changed Monaco side, but that form is already partly in the numbers. I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, 5.1 of them Monaco's, and already take 4% off Hearts for recent accuracy. Yesterday I took 3% off for Golovin's absence, but the numbers now count it, so I drop that cut and stay at 8.7.

401915813.overall: Iberia 1999 (29th of 36, 1 point) host Getafe (30th, 1 point) in Tbilisi, and both need a win to keep their hopes of the top 24 alive. Getafe are in trouble at home too: they lost 3-0 to Atlético on Sunday, sit 17th in LaLiga one point above the drop, and Djené was sent off late, though that ban is for LaLiga only. Zaid Romero has been cleared to play again, while Carvajal, Boselli, Juanmi and Uche are out and already in the numbers' missing list; Getafe rotate heavily in this competition and next play at Espanyol on Monday 30 November. Little news was available on Iberia beyond their poor recent attacking output, which the numbers count. No referee is named; I make no change.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 of them for Getafe. Getafe must win here, but they have not scored in their away league games and Bordalás may save players for the Espanyol game; the two roughly cancel, and the injured players are already in. I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, more of them Getafe's, and already add a little for Getafe's high recent corner count. Bordalás' direct, wide style is in their record. I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, already high for this competition and already up 9% for Iberia's recent bookings. Getafe's physical style under Bordalás is in their record, and Djené's red against Atlético only carries a LaLiga ban; no referee is named. I stay at 5.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and already add 7% to Getafe for their recent volume. Romero's return helps the back line rather than the attack, and I found nothing else to move it. I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target; Iberia have managed very few lately and Getafe's aim has been poor, both already counted. I stay at 8.1.

401915812.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored, 4 conceded), while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points after draws with Riga (1-1 on 5 Nov) and others and no win yet. Lugano lead the Swiss league despite a 5-0 loss at St. Gallen on 8 Nov and beat Grasshopper 2-1 on 21 Nov; they play a league game three days after this trip, and Mattia Croci-Torti rotated for the last European game (5 Nov, 3-0 over Zalgiris). Jablonec have regular keeper Jan Hanus out (Mihelak deputises; the numbers count it), captain Tekijaski is back, and Lugano still miss Hannes Delcroix (counted) with Dereck Moncada's hip knock from early November unclear. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and take about 16% off Lugano's scoring because they list Ajeti as suspended. That ban is domestic only (Swiss league, three games) and RSI says he can play in the Conference League, so I add part of it back to about 3.3; not all of it, because Croci-Torti rotates in Europe and Behrens may start instead. Jablonec's stand-in keeper for the injured Hanus is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec at home, and already count Lugano's slightly low recent corner count. Jablonec mostly played on the counter in their last home league game (0-0 with Mlada Boleslav), which fits the numbers rather than moving them, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.9 cards and already push both sides up for recent card-heavy games (Jablonec +9%, Lugano +5%). Ajeti's red at St. Gallen was a domestic matter and does not change the temperature here, and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots. Yesterday I trimmed this for Lugano rotation, but Ajeti being available gives a rotated side a proven forward, and Lugano have kept shooting freely with changed line-ups in Europe; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at about 30.7. Jablonec's recent shot counts are already in momentum.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already count Lugano's sharp recent finishing (35 on target in six). Moncada's status is still unclear but Ajeti's return to the European squad offsets that, so I now stay at about 9.2.

401915739.overall: A Baltic meeting in Kaunas between Kauno Zalgiris, last of 36 with 0 points and a 1-11 goal record (0-4 at Brighton, 1-4 at home to Brann, 0-3 at Lugano, where they had no shot on target until the 82nd minute), and Riga FC, 19th-20th after three draws (3 scored, 3 conceded). Both domestic seasons are over: Zalgiris won the Lithuanian title again and Riga finished second in Latvia, so neither side has played a competitive game since early November. Riga coach Adrian Gula said after the 1-1 with Jablonec that his side was tired after 50 matches since March; the break should freshen them but may also bring some rust. No injuries beyond Riga's two long-term absentees (Galo, Varslavans, already counted) and no referee were reported, and news for this match was thin, so the view rests on form and context.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already cut Zalgiris for scoring only 3 in their last six. I lean slightly lower to about 2.5: both teams come in with about three weeks without a competitive game, which tends to make for a slower, less sharp match; it is a mild hunch, not hard news.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.7 corners, 4.8 for Zalgiris at home, and already count their low recent corner count (4 in three). Nothing on tactics or line-ups points either way, so I stay at about 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.0 cards and already trim Riga sharply (-11.5%) for only 2 cards in their last three games and lift Zalgiris slightly. The Baltic-derby billing could add some edge, but no referee is named yet and neither side has a discipline story, so I stay at about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots and already count Riga's busy recent shooting and Zalgiris's low output (21 shots in three). Both sides should be at full strength with no domestic games to rest players for, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, already down for Zalgiris's 4 on target in their last three (they managed one at Lugano). I found no line-up or injury news that changes this, so I stay at about 8.4.

401915809.overall: Two sides near the bottom on 1 point each: Pafos are 30th-31st and Midtjylland 34th after a 6-1 home defeat to Ajax on 5 Nov, so both need a win to stay in the play-off race. Each is without a player sent off last time: Pafos lose Lele (25% of their goal involvement, which the numbers already take off) and Midtjylland lose Kjell Watjen; Midtjylland also have a long injury list (Castillo, keeper Bakker and several day-to-day players, all in the numbers' list), and one report has forward Mikael Uhre with a groin problem. Midtjylland, near the top of the Danish league, play at Brondby tonight (Monday 23 Nov) and at Copenhagen in a title clash on Sunday 29 Nov, so Mike Tullberg may rest players for this trip to Cyprus. Pafos (Ricardo Sa Pinto) won 2-1 at Omonia Aradippou on 21 Nov; no referee is named yet and specific team news was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already with Pafos cut about 19% for Lele's ban. I lean a little lower to about 2.4 because Midtjylland, wedged between Brondby away tonight and the title clash at Copenhagen, are likely to rotate, and one report has Uhre out with a groin problem; neither is in the numbers. Both teams' leaky recent defending is already in the momentum figures.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners and already add for both sides' high recent corner counts (Pafos conceded 52 in six). A rotated Midtjylland might sit deeper, which could cut both ways for corners, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.5 cards and already cut both sides about 9-10% for low recent card counts. Both teams had a player sent off last time (Lele, Watjen), which shows up in the bans rather than in a hotter match, and no referee is named, so I stay at about 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 12.6 for Midtjylland. I trim to about 26.8 since a rotated away side with Brondby just behind them and Copenhagen on Sunday is likely to take fewer shots; this schedule is not something the numbers count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already lifted for Pafos's sharp recent shooting (26 on target in six) and cut for Lele's ban. I lean slightly lower to about 9.4 for likely Midtjylland rotation and Uhre's reported injury.

401915808.overall: Brann are 6th-7th in the Conference League with 7 points and unbeaten in Europe (including 4-1 at Zalgiris), so a home win would put them close to a top-8 place. In Norway they won a wild 4-3 at KFUM on Sunday 22 Nov and host Kristiansund on 29 Nov; with little left at stake domestically, Europe should get their strongest side, though one report lists right-back Neraysho Kasanwirjo with a knee problem from that game, and their long injury list (Tronstad, Sorensen, Kjartansson and others) is already in the numbers. AGF are 24th on 2 points (one goal scored in three games) and have defender Frederik Tingager out for the rest of the autumn with a hamstring injury, which the numbers already know. No referee is named yet and news for this match was thin (fixture pages, match reports and club injury news), so the view rests on form and motivation.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.9 for Brann at home, and already count Brann's 16 goals in six and the absences of Gudmundsson and Tingager. Brann's 4-3 on Sunday fits their open style rather than adding anything new, and AGF have scored only once in three European games, so I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers expect 11.9 corners and already add for Brann's strong recent corner count (40 in six) and cut AGF's. I found no line-up or tactical news beyond that, so I stay at about 12.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.9 cards, 2.4 of them for AGF, and AGF's recent card rate is already counted. No referee is named yet and there is no rivalry edge between these clubs, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, with Brann at 18.5 and already lifted for their recent shooting and AGF's leaky defence. Brann's push for the top eight fits that picture rather than adding to it, and Kasanwirjo's knee problem (one report) is a full-back, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target and already lift Brann (34 on target in six) and trim AGF (8 in three). Nothing I found changes that, so I stay at about 10.6.

401915506.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) host Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, because Turkish authorities told UEFA the game could not be staged safely in Istanbul; fans are allowed in. Hapoel's team manager says about 13,000 tickets have gone to Besiktas fans and around 16,000 Turkish fans are expected in a stadium of about 20,000, so it should feel close to a home game. Besiktas won 4-2 at Konyaspor on Sunday (two from Vlahovic, plus Trossard and Cerny) and host leaders Galatasaray next in the league, but no rotation has been announced; centre-back Umit Akdag serves the second game of his two-match UEFA ban, which the numbers do not have. Hapoel are without Lucas Ventura and very likely Eliel Peretz plus Dan Biton, all already in the numbers' missing list. No referee is named yet; the news is small and points both ways, so I stay with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, about 2.2 for Besiktas and 0.7 for Hapoel, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.1%). Akdag's ban weakens Besiktas' back line a little, while Hapoel's missing midfielders (Peretz, Ventura) are already in the numbers; with a mostly Besiktas crowd expected in Batumi, the home edge is largely kept. I stay at about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and the neutral venue changes little for set pieces, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side. No referee is named yet; the political tension around the fixture is real and security will be heavy, but with almost no Israeli away support and a crowd of mainly Besiktas fans I see no clear push either way. I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas. With around 16,000 Turkish fans expected, the loss of the Istanbul crowd should cost little, and Besiktas' attack (Vlahovic, Trossard, Cerny) is scoring freely; the Galatasaray game next could bring some changes, but none are announced. I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 on target, 7.8 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for sharp recent finishing (+3.6%) and trim Hapoel's (-6.3%). The venue change and Akdag's ban do not change Besiktas' attack, so I stay at about 10.5.

401915519.overall: Celta (27th, 3 points) host Bournemouth (2nd, 12 points from four wins) at Balaidos. Bournemouth under Marco Rose keep winning, the latest 2-0 against Nottingham Forest, but Alex Toth and Juanlu Sanchez are out and Julian Araujo is unlikely (all in the numbers' missing list); Rose has said Alex Scott will start one of the Forest, Celta and Fulham games and Junior Kroupi is pushing to start, so some rotation is likely. Celta lost 2-1 at Real Madrid on Sunday and have won once in five; striker Borja Iglesias (soleus tear since mid-October) and Miguel Roman are still not ready and Carl Starfelt is close but waiting on tests, none of them in the numbers' missing list. Both sides play again on Sunday (Celta v Villarreal, Bournemouth at Fulham), and no referee is named yet. I keep a small lean lower on goals for Celta's blunt attack without Iglesias; the rest stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). Borja Iglesias, their main striker, is still out with a calf (soleus) tear and is not in the missing list, and Bournemouth may rotate a little with Fulham on Sunday; since much of his absence already shows in Celta's recent form, I only go mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, split fairly evenly. Bournemouth's direct, wide play and Celta's wing-backs both produce corners, and recent corner form is already in the numbers, so possible rotation on either side does not clearly change this. I stay at about 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already lower Bournemouth for being booked less lately (-5.2%). No referee is named yet; Yoel Lago's yellow-card ban is for Celta's league game, not this one, and nothing suggests a heated match, so I stay at about 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.3%), even if few go in. Possible Bournemouth rotation (Scott's minutes managed, Kroupi pushing to start) changes faces more than volume, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which partly reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth's in-form forward line, led by Evanilson, keeps their side of it up, so I stay at about 8.8.

401915517.overall: Dinamo Zagreb (9th, 7 points) host Bayer Leverkusen (7th, 9 points) at the Maksimir, both chasing the top-eight places. Dinamo have a new coach, Jerko Leko, who has won all three games in charge: 2-0 at Sunderland in this competition, 3-1 at Varazdin and 3-2 against Istra on Sunday. Captain Scott McKenna has been out since a training injury in late October and Robert Mudrazija is also injured; both are in the numbers' missing list and their absence already shows in Dinamo's recent results. Leverkusen won 4-0 against Paderborn and get Maza, Diaby, Tella and Kofane back, while Martin Terrier and Kennet Eichhorn remain out and Guela Doue is doubtful (all three in the missing list). No referee is named yet; with the absences already in the numbers, I now stay with the numbers on every stat (previously a small lean higher on goals).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.1 of them for Leverkusen. I had leaned slightly higher for McKenna's absence, but he is now in the numbers' missing list and has been out for about a month, during which Dinamo conceded fewer than expected; Leverkusen's returning forwards (Kofane, Diaby) only bring them back to full strength. I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.3 for Leverkusen, who have won a lot of corners lately (already counted, +1.6%). Leverkusen should have most of the ball as usual, and the coaching change at Dinamo has not changed how they play at home in a way the numbers miss, so I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, fairly even between the sides, and already nudge both up slightly for recent bookings. No referee is named yet; the Maksimir crowd can raise the temperature, but that is part of Dinamo's home record, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots and already lift Leverkusen for heavy recent shooting (+6.4%). Kofane and Diaby returning adds options while Terrier is still out, and Dinamo under Leko have been on the front foot, but nothing clearly moves the total, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 on target and already lift Leverkusen (+6.8%) after 45 on target in their last six. With the absences on both sides already in the missing list, I stay at about 9.9.

401915507.overall: Marseille (31st, 3 points) host Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) at the Velodrome and need a win to keep slim knockout hopes alive. Their four-game winning run ended on Sunday with a 3-2 home defeat by promoted Le Mans after leading 2-0; Bruno Genesio spoke of second-half collapses in the last three home games and missed Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, who was ill (no return date given, but illness is usually short). Emerson and Derek Cornelius are long-term absentees already in the numbers. Levski beat Lokomotiv Sofia 4-1 at the weekend, but key midfielder Serginho (4 goals, 8 assists) will probably miss the trip with a minor injury, and striker Stephane and Radoslav Kirilov are also out; only Kirilov is in the numbers' missing list. No referee is named yet; I lean slightly lower on goals and shots on target for Levski's weakened attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 2.4 for Marseille and 0.8 for Levski, and already lift Levski a little for Emerson's absence. Levski will likely be without Serginho, their main creator, and striker Stephane, neither in the missing list, which trims their small share; Marseille's late defensive lapses (3 conceded to Le Mans) are partly in their recent record already. I go mildly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 6.9 for Marseille. Levski usually defend deep away from home, which pushes corners Marseille's way, but that is in the numbers already, as is both teams' lower recent corner count. I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already lower Levski for few bookings lately (-5.1%) and raise Marseille (+4.9%). No referee is named yet; a frustrated Marseille side under pressure could pick up a card or two, but nothing concrete points that way, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, 18.6 for Marseille, already trimmed for their lower recent shot count (-6.9%). Marseille need the win and should have long spells of pressure, while Levski without Serginho may shoot less, but they rarely shoot much away anyway, so I stay at about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target, 7.2 for Marseille, and already trim Marseille for poor recent accuracy (-6.8%). Levski's attack loses Serginho and Stephane, which takes a little off their 2.9, so I go slightly lower, to about 9.9.

401915521.overall: Olympiacos are 6th in the Europa League with 10 points and unbeaten in five European games, and they warmed up with a 6-2 home win over Iraklis on Sunday, after which Imanol Alguacil said this attacking, chance-creating style is how he wants them to play. AC Milan are 28th with 3 points, but their Serie A form has turned (3-1 over Inter, 2-1 at Genoa, 5-1 over Frosinone on Sunday), and Ruben Amorim said they must win in Piraeus or qualifying becomes very complicated. Gonçalo Ramos went off early against Frosinone, but reports on 23 November say it was only fatigue and he is available. The numbers already take off Olympiacos' absentees (Chiquinho for about a week, Hezze, Puerta, El Kaabi, Yazici) and Milan's (Perera suspended, Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze); Tomori and Terracciano are doubtful and Leon Bailey is being checked after cramp against Iraklis. No referee is named yet; my small leans are a little more goals and cards because Milan have to chase the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals (1.0 Olympiacos, 1.1 Milan), already cut for Chiquinho and Hezze being out and nudged up for both sides' recent scoring. I lean a little higher, to about 2.3: Amorim has called this a must-win, Ramos is fit after only fatigue, and Olympiacos just scored six at home, so a cagey game seems less likely than the numbers assume.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Olympiacos, already adding for their busy wide play and taking off Milan's low recent count. Alguacil says his side attack down the flanks when the middle is closed, which is what the numbers see; Milan are without wide men Saelemaekers and Chukwueze, also already in their low count, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already trimmed for both sides' calm recent records. I lean slightly higher, to about 4.3: Milan must win to stay in the play-off race, Olympiacos want a top-eight place, and a full Karaiskakis tends to make these nights tense. No referee is named yet, so nothing on that side is counted.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.7 shots, 15.4 for Olympiacos and 9.4 for Milan, already adding for Olympiacos' busy attack and cutting Milan for their thin recent output. Milan's attack has picked up in Serie A, but that form is already part of the numbers, and Bailey's fitness is the only doubt in Olympiacos' front line, so I stay at about 25.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Milan's lower recent accuracy already taken off. Pulisic and Ramos are Milan's main threats and both should play, while Olympiacos lack El Kaabi but have Mouandilmadji and Armando González scoring; nothing new beyond what the numbers know, so I stay at about 8.

401915520.overall: RB Salzburg are 26th with 4 points and need to win, while Ararat-Armenia are last with no points after four games and lost their last European game 0-4 to AZ, though they have won their last three league games at home. Salzburg lost 1-0 at Austria Wien on Sunday, their first league defeat, with coach Danny Röhl suspended; Konate had a penalty saved early and, per ORF, Salzburg made few clear chances after that. Top scorer Haris Tabakovic (knee, out until January) is now in the numbers' missing list, along with Redzic (doubtful with a thigh problem), Kitano (ankle, not even registered for Europe), Boma, Mellberg, Schmid and Omoregie; together these cut Salzburg's expected goals sharply. Ararat lose goalkeeper João Bravim to a red-card ban, which the numbers also count. News on Ararat's squad was thin and no referee is named; since the numbers now know about Tabakovic, I drop my earlier goals trim and keep only a small cut to shots on target.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.5 for Salzburg, and they now take off Tabakovic, Redzic and Kitano while adding for Ararat playing without first-choice keeper Bravim. My earlier trim was for Tabakovic, which the numbers now count, so repeating it would be double counting; Redzic is listed as doubtful, which matches what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.6 corners, 5.3 for Salzburg. Losing a central striker changes who finishes moves more than how often Salzburg reach the byline, and Ararat should sit deep as the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already adding a little for Ararat's busy recent card count, which includes Bravim's red. Salzburg picked up three yellows in Vienna but that is their usual rate; no referee is named yet, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.7 shots, 18.8 for Salzburg, already adding for their busy recent attack. Against a bottom side with a reserve keeper Salzburg should still have the ball and take plenty of shots without Tabakovic, so volume should hold and I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, adding for Salzburg's sharp recent shooting; their missing players only change the goals number, not this one. I trim it slightly to about 10.0: that accuracy came largely through Tabakovic, and without him in Vienna Salzburg made few clear chances after Konate's saved penalty.

401915508.overall: Union Saint-Gilloise are 4th in the Europa League with 10 points and top of the Belgian league after a 1-0 win at Kortrijk on Sunday; David Hubert's side play this home game at Den Dreef in Leuven. Union were without defender Massiré Sylla at Kortrijk (unclear if injured or rested after a long Senegal trip) and Nikky Havenaar, with captain Kevin Mac Allister out long-term; Biondic's knock is already counted in the numbers. Lech Poznan lead the Polish league after a 1-0 win at GKS Katowice but have only 1 point in Europe, and Niels Frederiksen wants a win here or against Ferencvaros.
